title: A day longer than a year?

segments.text: A day is always shorter than a year. Well, that's not exactly true. On Venus, a day is longer than its year.
Venus spins incredibly slowly. One full turn takes about {243|two hundred forty three} Earth days.
But it goes around the sun in only {225|two hundred twenty five} days. So its year ends before a single spin is done.
Here's the wild part. Venus spins backwards. If you stood there, the sun would rise in the west and set in the east.
In fact, Venus is the hottest planet, even hotter than Mercury, which is closer to the sun. Its thick clouds trap the heat like a blanket.
That's not all. After the moon, Venus is the brightest thing in our night sky. You've probably seen it and thought it was a star.
So on Venus, you'd celebrate your birthday before the day was even over.
